'''''Sparaxis tricolor''''', known by the common names '''wandflower''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=SPTR|taxon=Sparaxis tricolor|access-date=24 November 2015}}</ref> '''harlequin flower''', and '''sparaxis''', is a [[bulb]]-forming [[perennial plant]] that grows in well-drained sunny soil. It gained its name from its colorful flowers which are bi- or tri-coloured with a golden centre and a small ring of brown surrounded by another colour.

The plant is native to the northern [[Bokkeveld Escarpment]] in the west-central [[Cape Provinces]] of [[South Africa]].<ref name = powo>{{cite web |title=''Sparaxis tricolor'' (Schneev.) Ker Gawl. |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:441392-1 |website=[[Plants of the World Online]] |publisher=[[Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew]] |access-date=27 May 2025}}</ref> It is present in [[California]] and Australia<ref name=APNI>{{cite web |url=http://www.anbg.gov.au/cgi-bin/apni?TAXON_NAME=Sparaxis+tricolor|title=''Sparaxis tricolor'' |access-date=18 March 2012 |work= [[Australian Plant Name Index]] (APNI), IBIS database|publisher = Centre for Plant Biodiversity Research, Australian Government, Canberra}}</ref> as an [[introduced species]] after having [[escaped plant|escaped from garden cultivation]].
